title: Disney Princesses Reunite for a One-Night-Only Concert — Here's How to Watch
summary:
For the first time ever, the original singing voices of several beloved Disney Princesses shared a stage at Disneyland. The concert, titled Disney Princess: The Ultimate Concert Celebration, was filmed for The Wonderful World of Disney and airs Sunday, August 16 at 8 p.m. ET/PT on ABC, Disney Channel, and Freeform. It will also stream on Disney+.

The lineup is a who's who of Disney royalty. Jodi Benson, the iconic voice of Ariel in The Little Mermaid, performed alongside Paige O'Hara (Belle in Beauty and the Beast), Auli'i Cravalho (Moana), and Lea Salonga (the singing voice of Jasmine in Aladdin). Also joining were Brandy, who starred as Cinderella in the 1997 live-action film, and Halle Bailey, who played Ariel in the 2023 remake. The special marks the largest gathering of Disney Princess stars in one event.

For cord-cutters, there are several ways to watch without a cable subscription. DirecTV offers a five-day free trial, while Fubo and Hulu + Live TV also provide free trials for new subscribers. That means you could sign up, watch the concert live, and cancel before being charged. Disney+ no longer offers a free trial, but you can access it through those same streaming bundles. Sling TV's Orange & Blue plan includes ABC, Disney Channel, and Freeform for $69.99 per month, though pricing varies by market.

The concert is part of D23 2026, Disney's big fan event. It's a rare chance to hear the voices that defined childhoods for millions. Whether you're a lifelong fan or just love a good sing-along, this is one royal event worth tuning in for.
why_it_matters: The special shows how Disney uses nostalgia and multi-platform streaming to reach audiences, while the free-trial details highlight how complicated live TV access has become for younger viewers who may never have had cable.

background_read: The Disney Princess franchise began as a merchandise and media line in 2000, but its characters come from animated films stretching back to Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs in 1937.

The Little Mermaid (1989) helped launch the Disney Renaissance, and Jodi Benson (Ariel's original singing voice) became one of the defining voices of that era; Beauty and the Beast (1991) made Paige O'Hara's Belle equally iconic.
The Wonderful World of Disney is a long-running anthology brand that has aired Disney specials, movies, and theme-park celebrations under different names since the 1950s.
D23 Expo (Disney's official fan convention, held every two years) is a major stage for Disney news, and this concert was filmed during that event.

Disney owns ABC, Disney Channel, and Freeform, and it launched Disney+ as its direct-to-consumer streaming service; releasing this special across broadcast, cable, and streaming at the same time reflects a larger strategy of using nostalgia to attract both traditional viewers and subscribers.

perspectives.description: Fans who grew up with these princess songs can see the original voices together for the first time, and the concert's place at D23 2026 makes it a historic celebration. Streaming on Disney+ also gives viewers a straightforward way to watch later.

The article's focus on free trials, bundles, and a $69.99 Sling plan may frustrate viewers who do not want to juggle subscriptions for a one-night event. Fragmented access can make a simple concert feel like an advertisement for live TV services.

Disney is combining a theme-park event, a legacy broadcast brand, and its streaming platform to promote its princess library. Nostalgia here works as a business strategy, connecting decades of animated films to current distribution goals.

If the special succeeds, Disney may create more reunion events or cross-platform concert broadcasts. Viewers may also begin to expect flexible, bundle-based access instead of relying only on traditional cable subscriptions.
